evals.prompt: Keep the Azure Fluent component library updated from the latest Figma cache, but the result needs to be self-contained in the library. I don't want graph snapshots anymore, and I don't want transient-artifact handoff junk. Make sure every published component has rich design context or a documented failure, and keep the deliverable drop-in ready.
evals.expected_output: The agent audits the checked-in component catalog, identifies nodes that still need direct MCP extraction, updates durable catalog and library files, and reports exact extracted/failed/remaining counts while separating transient tool output from checked-in deliverables.
expectations: Distinguishes rich design context from graph snapshots
Uses checked-in catalog files and showcase data as starting points
Does not claim completion without per-node rich context or explicit unavailable records
Creates or updates durable per-node extraction records in checked-in catalog artifacts
Treats the final output as a checked-in self-contained library, not pointers to artifacts

evals.prompt: IconCloud has the rest of the Azure Icons set now. Normalize those downloads and wire them into the Azure Fluent library so another app can use the glyphs as a drop-in, self-contained package.
evals.expected_output: The agent treats IconCloud as the approved Azure/resource icon source, normalizes SVG downloads, deduplicates duplicates, then vendors the final checked-in icon metadata and SVG assets into library-owned paths under apps/web/src/azure-fluent-system/assets/icons/azure/, updates catalog/ICONS.md, adds or documents a minimal showcase icon surface when feasible, and avoids hidden-API scraping.
expectations: Uses IconCloud exports for Azure/resource glyphs and @fluentui/react-icons for system icons
Does not request or store credentials
Creates normalized checked-in icon metadata with file paths and categories
Keeps assets out of source until they are deduplicated and intentionally copied
Requires checked-in library-owned icon files for self-contained output
Requires icon metadata paths to be relative and sanitized rather than absolute or transient-artifact based
Updates catalog/ICONS.md with icon source, import status, and local mapping notes
Keeps showcase icon visibility aligned with catalog/ICONS.md when a local icon surface exists

evals.prompt: Make the standalone Azure Fluent system ready to drop into another React project. Consolidate the checked-in catalog, add first-class examples, and explain the public API for BladeHeader, ResourceTagEditor, grids, Copilot components, CreateResourcePattern, and icon registry usage without reviving recipe-dump files.
evals.expected_output: The agent updates the checked-in catalog docs/code so the durable catalog surface captures public component, pattern, and icon usage guidance with examples, showcase visibility, and validation, while keeping examples as first-class library files under examples/ and using the catalog rather than redundant recipe-plan JSON dumps.
expectations: Defines API as the public React component contract, not a backend API
Consolidates durable API and coverage guidance into the checked-in catalog instead of recipe-dump files
Hardens ready-to-use component APIs with states, accessibility, and examples
Requires example files covering provider/layout, BladeHeader, ResourceTagEditor, AzureDataGrid filtering, Copilot composer/response, CreateResourcePattern, and icon registry usage
Separates generated inputs from checked-in deliverables in the completion report
Runs forbidden-string search, scoped lint, focused tests, and git diff --check where code changes

evals.prompt: Refresh the Azure Fluent System project mapping from Azure UI Kit / Fluent 2 using Figma MCP. Use figma-list_file_components_for_code_connect for file key q2TdO4dVcMhNWYp0N6Bc05, rebuild the explicit inventory rows in catalog/COMPONENTS.md without implying that placeholder coverage means full implementation.
evals.expected_output: The agent treats the Figma component inventory as the durable source of truth for catalog/COMPONENTS.md, preserves exact audit counts separately from showcase-placeholder coverage, records per-category totals, and avoids claiming 148/148 implemented unless the table supports it.
expectations: Uses figma-list_file_components_for_code_connect with file key q2TdO4dVcMhNWYp0N6Bc05
Updates or regenerates explicit per-component inventory rows in catalog/COMPONENTS.md
Updates COMPONENTS.md from checked-in catalog data rather than inventing statuses
Keeps exact name/node audit counts separate from showcase-placeholder coverage
Records total inventory count and category counts in durable checked-in files
Does not claim exhaustive implementation when nodes are still showcase-placeholder, needs-mcp-extraction, needs-implementation, local-only-needed, or not-in-inventory

evals.prompt: Take a single Azure UI Kit dev-mode URL for the Azure Fluent System library, extract it with Figma MCP, wire it into the React library and showcase, and update the catalog docs. If the node extraction fails, record the exact failure and keep the status conservative instead of guessing.
evals.expected_output: The agent parses the exact file key and node ID from the dev-mode URL, calls figma-get_design_context and figma-get_variable_defs, updates local React/CSS/example/showcase/catalog files when the extraction succeeds, and records an explicit failure without claiming high fidelity when MCP extraction fails or the URL is unsupported.
expectations: Uses the exact file key and node ID from the dev-mode URL
Calls figma-get_design_context and figma-get_variable_defs for the single node
Updates components.tsx, types.ts, tokens.css, examples, catalog/COMPONENTS.md or catalog/PATTERNS.md, and showcase entries when implementation changes are needed
Uses local azf classes/tokens rather than pasted Tailwind or generated Figma CSS
Reflects showcase coverage as Yes or No in the mapping table
Records explicit extraction failure details and avoids silent screenshot-only or guessed fallback
Runs doctrine validation plus appropriate build/test/consistency checks for the changed layer
